subject: how to use facet to "zoom" part of a time series?

messages.author: 3b1b96295b24408a
messages.subject: how to use facet to "zoom" part of a time series?
parts:
I'm trying to tackle the following: consider weekly measurements
between 1990 and 2005. Annual statistics shall be visualised with a
sequence of boxplots. The years 1998-2000 stand out by their generally
high values.

Facetting by year allows me to single out the period 1998-2000 so that
its high values won't flatten down all the remaining boxplots. There
will thus be three facet for the periods 1990-97, 98-00, and 2001 and
later

While facet_wrap offers to separate the y-axes (and have them adjusted
to the different y-ranges), it will allot equal horizontal space to
each of the periods: 1990-97 will show narrow boxes (all have to fit
into the facet), 1998-00 wide boxes (only three years to occupy the
panel width) and so on.

Facet_grid, in turn, allows to define "space=free" and have the facet
width automatically adjust to the number of categories contained.
However, in facet_grid, all facets of a row have to share one y-axis.
Which was to be avoided in the first place.

Any suggestions greatly appreciated. I'm not too familiar with the
ggplot2 grammar yet, so I guess I'm just missing some straightforward
solution. After all, the package seems to be the coolest plotting tool
around!

best regards
Ivo
